content.text:
Confirmed: before commit 54a35c3b, there was no in-memory `Set<Alarm>` of alarms at all — `enable()`/`set()` just wrote to the DB and `disableExpiredAlarms()` iterated a fresh `Cursor`, so there was nothing to mutate during iteration. Commit 54a35c3b introduced the `set` field, made `changeAlarm()` do `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm)`, and changed `disableExpiredAlarms()` to iterate over that same `set` while calling `enable()` (→ `changeAlarm()`) inside the loop — a `ConcurrentModificationException` waiting to happen whenever an alarm needed to be disabled at startup. This exact pattern persisted (through the `Alarms.java` split and later renamed to `init()`) until commit 6a2dd27 fixed it by no longer routing through `enable()`/`changeAlarm()` inside the loop.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 54a35c3bc3a56e686bd09d3854528bb056e26740

## Reasoning
(1) I diffed the fix commit `6a2dd27` and saw the key change was replacing `enable(alarm.getId(), false)` (called from inside a `for (Alarm alarm : set)` loop) with a direct `alarm.setEnabled(false); writeToDb(...)` call that doesn't touch `set`. I then used `git log -p --follow` on `Alarms.java`/`AlarmsManager.java` to trace when this loop-calls-enable-which-mutates-set pattern first appeared.

(2) Commit `54a35c3b` ("Alarm: refactoring") introduced an in-memory `Set<Alarm> set` field loaded once from the DB, changed `changeAlarm()`/`enable()` to do `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);` (mutating that set), and rewrote `disableExpiredAlarms()` to iterate `for (Alarm alarm : set) { ... enable(alarm.getId(), false); ... }`.
